718	/-- **The identity component inclusion is a group-scheme homomorphism.**
719	
720	Kleiman §5 Lem.~`lem:agps`~(3) conclusion (b): the clopen subscheme `G^0`
721	inherits a `k`-group-scheme structure from `G`, and the inclusion morphism
722	`G^0 ↪ G` (from `IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme`) is compatible
723	with the group laws on source and target. The statement asserts the
724	existence of the inherited `GrpObj` structure; the compatibility of
725	the inclusion with the group operations is the substantive content of
726	Kleiman's argument (the product `G^0 ×_k G^0` is connected by
727	EGA IV₂ 4.5.8; the group-multiplication map sends this connected subset
728	containing the identity into the connected component `G^0`).
729	
730	The proof applies `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` to the subgroup presheaf
731	`identityComponentSubgroupFunctor`: the group structure on `Hom(T, G⁰)` is
732	the subgroup of `Hom(T, G)` of morphisms landing in the carrier, with closure
733	under `mul`/`inv` provided by the connectedness core lemmas
734	`range_tensor_mul_subset` / `range_inclusion_inv_subset` above. The induced
735	group law on `G⁰` is by construction compatible with the inclusion (the
736	Yoneda equivalence is `u ↦ u ≫ identityComponentInclusion G`). -/
737	theorem IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism {k : Type u} [Field k]

739	    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
740	    Nonempty (GrpObj (IdentityComponent G)) :=
741	  ⟨GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy (IdentityComponent G) (identityComponentSubgroupFunctor G)

744	/-! ### Finite type and geometric irreducibility of `G⁰`
745	
746	Kleiman §5 Lem.~`lem:agps`~(3) conclusion (c). The argument follows Kleiman's
747	translation trick (closed-point translation via `GrpObj.mulRight`, closed
748	points ↔ rational points via `pointEquivClosedPoint`, Jacobson density of
749	closed points), in the form used by Mathlib for
750	`smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed` in
751	`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Smooth.lean`.
752	
753	Layer structure:
754	1. `irreducibleSpace_of_connectedSpace_of_nhds` — EGA I 6.1.10 in topological
755	   form: a connected space in which every point has an irreducible open
756	   neighbourhood is irreducible.
757	2. `identityComponent_irreducibleSpace_of_isAlgClosed` /
758	   `identityComponent_compactSpace_of_isAlgClosed` — the geometric core over
759	   an algebraically closed field: translate a nonempty irreducible (resp.
760	   quasi-compact affine) open through every closed point using the inherited
761	   group structure of `G⁰` (`isSubgroupHomomorphism`), then sweep up the
762	   non-closed points by Jacobson density.
763	3. `identityComponent_compactSpace` /
764	   `identityComponent_geometricallyIrreducible` (placed after
765	   `baseChangeIso` below) — descent to an arbitrary base field along the
766	   surjective projection from the base change to the algebraic closure,
767	   using `baseChangeIso` to identify `(G_K̄)⁰` with the base change of `G⁰`.
768	
769	The theorem `isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible` is assembled from these
770	after `baseChangeIso`. -/
771	
772	/-- **EGA I 6.1.10** (topological form): a connected topological space in
773	which every point admits an irreducible open neighbourhood is irreducible.
774	
775	Proof: let `Z` be the irreducible component of some point. For `z ∈ Z` pick
776	an irreducible open `V ∋ z`; then `Z ∩ V` is nonempty, so
777	`Z ⊆ closure (Z ∩ V) ⊆ closure V` (a nonempty open subset of a
778	preirreducible set is dense in it); `closure V` is irreducible, so
779	maximality of `Z` forces `closure V = Z`, whence `V ⊆ Z` and `Z` is open.
780	Components are always closed, so the nonempty clopen `Z` is everything by
781	connectedness. -/
782	private lemma irreducibleSpace_of_connectedSpace_of_nhds
783	    {α : Type*} [TopologicalSpace α] [ConnectedSpace α]
784	    (h : ∀ x : α, ∃ V : Set α, IsOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧ IsIrreducible V) :
785	    IrreducibleSpace α := by
786	  obtain ⟨x₀⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty α)
787	  have hZmem : Maximal IsIrreducible (irreducibleComponent x₀) :=
788	    irreducibleComponent_mem_irreducibleComponents x₀
789	  have hZopen : IsOpen (irreducibleComponent x₀) := by
790	    rw [isOpen_iff_mem_nhds]
791	    intro z hz
792	    obtain ⟨V, hVopen, hzV, hVirr⟩ := h z
793	    have h1 : irreducibleComponent x₀ ⊆ closure V :=
794	      (subset_closure_inter_of_isPreirreducible_of_isOpen hZmem.prop.2 hVopen
795	        ⟨z, hz, hzV⟩).trans (closure_mono Set.inter_subset_right)
796	    have h2 : closure V = irreducibleComponent x₀ :=
797	      hZmem.eq_of_superset hVirr.closure h1
798	    exact mem_nhds_iff.mpr ⟨V, h2 ▸ subset_closure, hVopen, hzV⟩
799	  have hZuniv : irreducibleComponent x₀ = Set.univ :=
800	    (isClopen_iff.mp ⟨isClosed_irreducibleComponent, hZopen⟩).resolve_left
801	      (Set.Nonempty.ne_empty ⟨x₀, mem_irreducibleComponent⟩)
802	  haveI : PreirreducibleSpace α := ⟨hZuniv ▸ hZmem.prop.2⟩
803	  exact ⟨⟨x₀⟩⟩

806	type: it is the composite of the open immersion `G⁰ ↪ G` with `G.hom`. -/

809	    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
810	    LocallyOfFiniteType (IdentityComponent G).hom := by
811	  change LocallyOfFiniteType ((identityComponentCarrier G).ι ≫ G.hom)

814	/-- Existence of a nonempty irreducible open subset of `|G⁰|`: inside any
815	affine open `W` (a Noetherian space, since `G⁰` is locally Noetherian over
816	the field `k`), the complement of the union of the irreducible components of
817	`W` other than a fixed one is open, nonempty, and contained in that fixed
818	irreducible component (Stacks 0052 (3)); its image under the open embedding
819	`W ↪ G⁰` is the required open. -/
820	private lemma identityComponent_exists_isOpen_nonempty_isIrreducible
821	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (G : Over (Spec (.of k)))
822	    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
823	    ∃ U : Set (IdentityComponent G).left,
824	      IsOpen U ∧ U.Nonempty ∧ IsIrreducible U := by
825	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (IdentityComponent G).hom :=
826	    identityComponent_locallyOfFiniteType G
827	  haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian (IdentityComponent G).left :=
828	    LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (IdentityComponent G).hom
829	  obtain ⟨x₀⟩ : Nonempty (IdentityComponent G).left := inferInstance
830	  obtain ⟨W, hW, hx₀W, -⟩ := exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset
831	    (X := (IdentityComponent G).left) (U := ⊤)
832	    (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_top x₀)
833	  haveI : IsNoetherianRing Γ((IdentityComponent G).left, W) :=
834	    IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian ⟨W, hW⟩
835	  haveI : TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace ↥W := noetherianSpace_of_isAffineOpen W hW
836	  obtain ⟨o, hoopen, hone, hoZ⟩ :=
837	    TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.exists_isOpen_nonempty_subset_irreducibleComponent
838	      (irreducibleComponent (⟨x₀, hx₀W⟩ : ↥W))
839	      (irreducibleComponent_mem_irreducibleComponents _)
840	  have hoirr : IsIrreducible o :=
841	    ⟨hone, (isIrreducible_irreducibleComponent
842	      (x := (⟨x₀, hx₀W⟩ : ↥W))).2.open_subset hoopen hoZ⟩
843	  exact ⟨(Subtype.val : ↥W → (IdentityComponent G).left) '' o,
844	    W.isOpen.isOpenMap_subtype_val _ hoopen, hone.image _,
845	    hoirr.image _ continuous_subtype_val.continuousOn⟩

859	algebraically closed field**: over `K = K̄` the identity component `G⁰` is
860	irreducible. Translate one nonempty irreducible open `U` (which exists by

862	closed point `z` via the translation isomorphism `x ↦ x·g⁻¹·z` (with `g` a
863	closed point of `U`, so that the translate contains `z`); Jacobson density
864	sweeps up the non-closed points; conclude by EGA I 6.1.10 and connectedness
865	of `G⁰`. -/
866	private theorem identityComponent_irreducibleSpace_of_isAlgClosed
867	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]
868	    (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
869	    IrreducibleSpace (IdentityComponent G).left := by
870	  letI : GrpObj (IdentityComponent G) :=
871	    Classical.choice (IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism G)

875	    LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace (IdentityComponent G).hom

877	    identityComponent_exists_isOpen_nonempty_isIrreducible G
878	  obtain ⟨g, hgU, hgc⟩ := nonempty_inter_closedPoints hUne hUopen.isLocallyClosed
879	  let g' : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ IdentityComponent G :=
880	    Over.homMk _ ((pointEquivClosedPoint (IdentityComponent G).hom).symm ⟨g, hgc⟩).2
881	  have hg' : ∀ a, g'.left a = g := fun a => by simp [g', pointEquivClosedPoint]
882	  let pt : ↥(𝟙_ (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))).left :=
883	    (default : ↥(Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
884	  have hcover : ∀ z ∈ closedPoints (IdentityComponent G).left,
885	      ∃ V : Set (IdentityComponent G).left, IsOpen V ∧ z ∈ V ∧ IsIrreducible V := by
886	    intro z hzc
887	    let z' : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ IdentityComponent G :=
888	      Over.homMk _ ((pointEquivClosedPoint (IdentityComponent G).hom).symm ⟨z, hzc⟩).2
889	    have hz' : ∀ a, z'.left a = z := fun a => by simp [z', pointEquivClosedPoint]
890	    -- the right-translation `x ↦ x·(g⁻¹·z)`, an automorphism sending `g` to `z`
891	    let τ : IdentityComponent G ⟶ IdentityComponent G :=
892	      (GrpObj.mulRight (A := IdentityComponent G) (g'⁻¹ * z')).hom
893	    haveI hτiso : IsIso τ :=
894	      inferInstanceAs (IsIso (GrpObj.mulRight (A := IdentityComponent G) (g'⁻¹ * z')).hom)
895	    haveI : IsIso τ.left :=
896	      inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((Over.forget (Spec (.of K))).map τ))
897	    have hτ : g' ≫ τ = z' := by
898	      rw [show g' ≫ τ =
899	          g' ≫ (GrpObj.mulRight (A := IdentityComponent G) (g'⁻¹ * z')).hom from rfl,
900	        comp_mulRight_hom]
901	      exact mul_inv_cancel_left g' z'
902	    have hτl : g'.left ≫ τ.left = z'.left := by
903	      simpa using
904	        congrArg (fun q : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ IdentityComponent G => q.left) hτ
905	    have hτ' : τ.left g = z := by
906	      calc τ.left g = τ.left (g'.left pt) := by rw [hg' pt]
907	        _ = (g'.left ≫ τ.left) pt := (Scheme.Hom.comp_apply _ _ _).symm
908	        _ = z'.left pt := by rw [hτl]
909	        _ = z := hz' pt
910	    exact ⟨⇑τ.left '' U, τ.left.isOpenEmbedding.isOpenMap _ hUopen,
911	      ⟨g, hgU, hτ'⟩, hUirr.image _ (Scheme.Hom.continuous τ.left).continuousOn⟩

913	      IsOpen V ∧ IsIrreducible V}) :=

915	  have hsU : ⋃₀ {V : Set (IdentityComponent G).left | IsOpen V ∧ IsIrreducible V} =

930	/-- **Kleiman §5 Lem.~`lem:agps`~(3)(c), quasi-compactness core over an
931	algebraically closed field**: over `K = K̄` the identity component `G⁰` is
932	quasi-compact. Let `W ∋ e` be an affine open. For a closed point `z`, the
933	preimage `χ_z⁻¹(W)` of `W` under the "division" morphism `χ_z : x ↦ x⁻¹·z`
934	contains `z` (because `χ_z(z) = e ∈ W`), so it meets `W` in a nonempty open
935	(`G⁰` is irreducible by the previous lemma), which contains a closed point
936	`g` by Jacobson density; then `u := g⁻¹·z` is a rational point landing in
937	`W` and `z = g·u` lies in the image of the multiplication
938	`m : W ×_K W ⟶ G⁰`. So the compact `m(W ×_K W)` contains all closed points;
939	finitely many affine opens cover it, and by Jacobson density they cover
940	everything. -/
941	private theorem identityComponent_compactSpace_of_isAlgClosed
942	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]
943	    (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
944	    CompactSpace (IdentityComponent G).left := by
945	  letI : GrpObj (IdentityComponent G) :=
946	    Classical.choice (IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism G)
947	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (IdentityComponent G).hom :=
948	    identityComponent_locallyOfFiniteType G
949	  haveI : JacobsonSpace (IdentityComponent G).left :=
950	    LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace (IdentityComponent G).hom
951	  haveI : IrreducibleSpace (IdentityComponent G).left :=
952	    identityComponent_irreducibleSpace_of_isAlgClosed G
953	  -- an affine open around the identity point
954	  obtain ⟨W, hW, heW, -⟩ := exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset
955	    (X := (IdentityComponent G).left) (U := ⊤)
956	    (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_top (identitySectionPoint (IdentityComponent G)))
957	  haveI hWc : CompactSpace W.toScheme := isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp hW.isCompact
958	  haveI : QuasiCompact (W.ι ≫ (IdentityComponent G).hom) :=
959	    HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr hWc
960	  let UW : Over (Spec (.of K)) := Over.mk (W.ι ≫ (IdentityComponent G).hom)
961	  let ιU : UW ⟶ IdentityComponent G := Over.homMk W.ι rfl
962	  let m : UW ⊗ UW ⟶ IdentityComponent G :=
963	    (ιU ⊗ₘ ιU) ≫ MonObj.mul (X := IdentityComponent G)
964	  haveI : CompactSpace (UW ⊗ UW).left :=
965	    inferInstanceAs (CompactSpace ↥(pullback (W.ι ≫ (IdentityComponent G).hom)
966	      (W.ι ≫ (IdentityComponent G).hom)))
967	  let pt : ↥(𝟙_ (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))).left :=
968	    (default : ↥(Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
969	  -- all closed points lie in the image of `m`
970	  have hmem : ∀ z ∈ closedPoints (IdentityComponent G).left,
971	      z ∈ Set.range ⇑m.left := by
972	    intro z hzc
973	    let z' : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ IdentityComponent G :=
974	      Over.homMk _ ((pointEquivClosedPoint (IdentityComponent G).hom).symm ⟨z, hzc⟩).2
975	    have hz' : ∀ a, z'.left a = z := fun a => by simp [z', pointEquivClosedPoint]
976	    -- the "division" morphism `x ↦ x⁻¹·z`
977	    let χ : IdentityComponent G ⟶ IdentityComponent G :=
978	      GrpObj.inv (X := IdentityComponent G) ≫
979	        (GrpObj.mulRight (A := IdentityComponent G) z').hom
980	    have hχ : ∀ p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ IdentityComponent G,
981	        p ≫ χ = p⁻¹ * z' := fun p => by
982	      rw [show p ≫ χ = (p ≫ GrpObj.inv (X := IdentityComponent G)) ≫
983	            (GrpObj.mulRight (A := IdentityComponent G) z').hom from
984	          (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm,
985	        ← Hom.inv_def, comp_mulRight_hom]
986	    have hone : (1 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ IdentityComponent G) =
987	        MonObj.one (X := IdentityComponent G) := by
988	      rw [Hom.one_def, toUnit_unique (toUnit _) (𝟙 _), Category.id_comp]
989	    -- `χ` sends `z` to the identity point, which lies in `W`
990	    have hχz : χ.left z = identitySectionPoint (IdentityComponent G) := by
991	      have h1 : z'.left ≫ χ.left = (MonObj.one (X := IdentityComponent G)).left := by
992	        simpa using
993	          congrArg (fun q : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ IdentityComponent G => q.left)
994	            ((hχ z').trans (by rw [inv_mul_cancel, hone]))
995	      calc χ.left z = χ.left (z'.left pt) := by rw [hz' pt]
996	        _ = (z'.left ≫ χ.left) pt := (Scheme.Hom.comp_apply _ _ _).symm
997	        _ = (MonObj.one (X := IdentityComponent G)).left pt := by rw [h1]
998	        _ = identitySectionPoint (IdentityComponent G) := rfl
999	    have hχzW : χ.left z ∈ (W : Set (IdentityComponent G).left) := hχz ▸ heW
1000	    -- a closed point in `W ∩ χ⁻¹(W)`
1001	    have hinter : ((W : Set (IdentityComponent G).left) ∩
1002	        ⇑χ.left ⁻¹' (W : Set (IdentityComponent G).left)).Nonempty :=
1003	      nonempty_preirreducible_inter W.isOpen
1004	        (W.isOpen.preimage (Scheme.Hom.continuous χ.left)) ⟨_, heW⟩ ⟨z, hχzW⟩
1005	    obtain ⟨g, ⟨hgW, hgE⟩, hgc⟩ := nonempty_inter_closedPoints hinter
1006	      (W.isOpen.inter
1007	        (W.isOpen.preimage (Scheme.Hom.continuous χ.left))).isLocallyClosed
1008	    let g' : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ IdentityComponent G :=
1009	      Over.homMk _ ((pointEquivClosedPoint (IdentityComponent G).hom).symm ⟨g, hgc⟩).2
1010	    have hg' : ∀ a, g'.left a = g := fun a => by simp [g', pointEquivClosedPoint]
1011	    -- `u := g⁻¹·z` is a rational point landing in `W`
1012	    have hu : ∀ a, (g'⁻¹ * z').left a = χ.left g := fun a => by
1013	      have h1 : g'.left ≫ χ.left = (g'⁻¹ * z').left := by
1014	        simpa using
1015	          congrArg (fun q : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ IdentityComponent G => q.left)
1016	            (hχ g')
1017	      calc (g'⁻¹ * z').left a = (g'.left ≫ χ.left) a := by rw [h1]
1018	        _ = χ.left (g'.left a) := Scheme.Hom.comp_apply _ _ _
1019	        _ = χ.left g := by rw [hg' a]
1020	    -- factor `g'` and `u := g'⁻¹ * z'` through `W`
1021	    have hrg : Set.range ⇑g'.left ⊆ Set.range ⇑W.ι := by
1022	      rw [Scheme.Opens.range_ι]
1023	      rintro - ⟨a, rfl⟩
1024	      rw [hg' a]; exact hgW
1025	    have hru : Set.range ⇑(g'⁻¹ * z').left ⊆ Set.range ⇑W.ι := by
1026	      rw [Scheme.Opens.range_ι]
1027	      rintro - ⟨a, rfl⟩
1028	      rw [hu a]; exact hgE
1029	    let gW : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ UW :=
1030	      Over.homMk (IsOpenImmersion.lift W.ι g'.left hrg) (by
1031	        change IsOpenImmersion.lift W.ι g'.left hrg ≫
1032	          W.ι ≫ (IdentityComponent G).hom = _
1033	        rw [← Category.assoc, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac W.ι g'.left hrg]
1034	        exact Over.w g')
1035	    let uW : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ UW :=
1036	      Over.homMk (IsOpenImmersion.lift W.ι (g'⁻¹ * z').left hru) (by
1037	        change IsOpenImmersion.lift W.ι (g'⁻¹ * z').left hru ≫
1038	          W.ι ≫ (IdentityComponent G).hom = _
1039	        rw [← Category.assoc, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac W.ι (g'⁻¹ * z').left hru]
1040	        exact Over.w (g'⁻¹ * z'))
1041	    have hgWι : gW ≫ ιU = g' := by
1042	      apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
1043	      exact IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac W.ι g'.left hrg
1044	    have huWι : uW ≫ ιU = g'⁻¹ * z' := by
1045	      apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
1046	      exact IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac W.ι (g'⁻¹ * z').left hru
1047	    have hfin : lift gW uW ≫ m = z' := by
1048	      change lift gW uW ≫ (ιU ⊗ₘ ιU) ≫ MonObj.mul (X := IdentityComponent G) = z'

13	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`), and
14	it settles it in the direction opposite to what that file's docstring and the
15	board row `AJC.picrep.etale-rep` currently assert.
16	
17	## The claim this file refutes
18	
19	Clause (1) of the seam asks for representability of the étale-sheafified
20	functor `PicScheme.picEt C`, while every milestone of the Milne–Kollár campaign
21	targets the *unsheafified* `PicScheme.picSharp C`. The seam docstring and the
22	board row both say the gap between them **cannot be bridged without a
23	`k`-rational point**, on the grounds that the comparison
24	`PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 — an isomorphism only under
25	a section — and that a section is exactly what the owner decision `I-0491`
26	forbids the headline to carry.
27	
28	That reasoning is wrong, and the error is a direction confusion. Kleiman §2
29	Thm 2.5 is the statement that a section makes the comparison an isomorphism
30	*with no hypothesis on the presheaf*. But there is a second, entirely
31	independent, route to the same conclusion: the comparison is the sheafification
32	unit, and a unit is an isomorphism **exactly when its source is already a
33	sheaf** (`CategoryTheory.isIso_toSheafify`). A representable functor is a sheaf
34	for any subcanonical topology. So *if* the campaign delivers representability of
35	`picSharp`, the source is a sheaf for that reason alone, the unit is an
36	isomorphism, and no section is involved anywhere.
37	
38	The consequence for the route, stated precisely because the board row is
39	currently priced on its negation: the campaign's endpoint **is** transportable
40	to clause (1). `picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` below is that
41	transport, proved with no rational-point hypothesis of any kind.
42	
43	## What is actually still open
44	
45	This file does **not** close the seam. It removes an alleged obstruction, which
46	is a different thing, and the honest statement of what remains is:
47	
48	* the antecedent of every theorem here is representability of `picSharp C`
49	  over an arbitrary field — campaign milestones J1–J5, G3, G4, B1/B4/B6,
50	  D2′–D4′, P5 — and **not one of those is discharged**. No theorem in this file
51	  is applied to a curve anywhere in the project, and none should be reported as
52	  progress on the existence question;
53	* what changes is the *shape* of the remaining work. Before this file, a reader
54	  of the seam docstring concluded that finishing the campaign leaves a further
55	  unpriced obligation ("represent `picEt` directly, or restate the headline").
56	  After it, no supplementary étale-representability theorem is needed: `picEt`
57	  representability follows from `picSharp` representability by `Subcanonical` +
58	  `isIso_toSheafify`, both already in Mathlib.
59	
60	**But the antecedent must not be read as reachable over `k`, and §4 is why.**
61	The same subcanonicity that powers the transport also proves that a
62	representable `picSharp` is a *Zariski* sheaf
63	(`PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy`).
64	
65	**But the falsity of `picSharp` representability is quoted from Kleiman, NOT
66	derived from that theorem** — corrected 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc` / `I-0970`,
67	after two successive citations in this slot turned out not to support it).
68	Kleiman L5105–L5108: for the conic `u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ` — smooth, proper,
69	geometrically integral, no rational point, i.e. exactly these binders —
70	`Pic_{X/ℝ}` is **not representable**, while `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` is by §4 `th:main`.
71	That is direct. The Zariski route would need "`picSharp` is not a Zariski
72	sheaf", which no source establishes: `ex:Pfs` compares the two *sheafifications*
73	`zar` and `ét` (both already sheaves), and `th:cmp` part 1 gives
74	`picSharp ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` here, so `picSharp` is Zariski-*separated* and any
75	failure could only be gluing. Do **not** rebuild the argument that way.
76	Contrapositive of the quoted fact: representability of `picSharp C` over an
77	arbitrary field is **false in general**, not merely unproved. So the campaign
78	milestones that conclude representability of `picSharp`/`picSharpDeg` over `k`
79	itself — G3 (Galois descent of `picSharp` points) and G4 (the coproduct
80	assembly) — aim at a statement that cannot be proved as written.
81	
82	This is not an argument against the Milne–Kollár route. Everything through J5
83	runs over a separably closed `k'`, where a section is available and the
84	obstruction is absent; the break is precisely at the descent step where the
85	conclusion returns to `k`. The repair the results here name is that the object
86	descended to `k` must be `picEt` and not `picSharp`. Over `k'` the two agree, by
87	`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf` applied to the representability available
88	there — so J5's output is already a `picEt`-representing scheme after base
89	change.
90	
91	**§4 makes the constraint a reduction rather than a quotation**, which is the
92	one place this file goes beyond restating Kleiman.
93	`not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison` proves: if the
94	comparison fails to be an isomorphism then NO scheme represents `picSharp C`.
95	That is Kleiman's own inference at L5105–L5108 ("the two functors differ, so
96	`Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable") supplied with a proof, and it is the
97	contrapositive of §3 — no sheaf step, no topology. So a hypothetical proof of
98	G3/G4 as written would prove `picEtComparison` is an isomorphism for *every*
99	curve over *every* field, including pointless ones.
100	
101	What is **not** formalised, and is the whole residue of the argument: that the
102	comparison genuinely fails for that conic. Kleiman's `φ*O(1)` witness runs
103	through `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ` and flat base change. Producing it in Lean is bounded,
104	well-specified work, and §4's theorems are the interface it plugs into. Until
105	then "G3/G4 target a false statement" rests on that one quotation — and on
106	nothing else, which is the improvement.
107	
108	There is one genuine subtlety, and it is not a section. The transport proves
109	that the *same* scheme represents both functors, so it does not produce
110	`picSharp` representability out of nothing — it consumes it. Read
111	`Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` as: the campaign does not
112	need a supplementary étale-representability theorem, only the subcanonicity
113	lemma proved here.
